title: Records Dashboard Overview
summary: Defines inventory semantics, grouping behavior, and record card interpretation for daily operations.
coverage: Record card fields and status signals
When to use grouped vs flat list view

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Records is the source of truth for internet-facing inventory metadata in RAPTOR. Dashboard and security interpretations depend on record quality and ownership completeness.

sections.title: Inventory purpose
paragraphs: The Records dashboard is the operational inventory layer for all tracked internet-facing assets. It centralizes DNS asset metadata, ownership context, and application grouping so operators can maintain an accurate, actionable view of external exposure.

Use this page as the primary entry point for metadata validation, lifecycle cleanup, and ownership correction. Do not treat it as a static reference. It is designed for continuous operational maintenance.

sections.title: List organization model
paragraphs: Records can be displayed in grouped mode or flat mode. Grouped mode organizes entries by application and is best for ownership and service-level review. Flat mode is best for rapid multi-record triage or broad search validation.
Sort order follows recent modification and creation timestamps so current operational changes appear first.

rows: Application-level ownership, governance review, release impact checks.
Shows service context and record concentration by app boundary.
Large filter result triage and rapid metadata correction.
Reduces navigation overhead for high-volume edits.

sections.title: Record card semantics
paragraphs: Each record card represents a single DNS asset and exposes core metadata fields needed by operators, security teams, and managers. Expand the card to inspect details and edit permitted fields.
The record card is intentionally compact in collapsed state and operational in expanded state. This allows fast scanning while preserving full edit capability where needed.

Defines who accepts risk and remediation priority.
Defines who executes technical change and remediation updates.
Provides initial attack surface context for testing and review.

sections.title: Operational review rhythm
paragraphs: For healthy inventory operations, run record review as a repeatable cycle. Teams should validate newly changed records first, then resolve missing ownership and stale technical metadata.
A practical weekly sequence is to filter by recent changes, validate assignment fields, verify open ports formatting, and export exceptions for cross-team follow-up.

tip.title: TIP
paragraphs: When using grouped mode, collapse stable applications and focus only on groups with recent changes or ownership gaps to reduce review time.

sections.title: Cross-module impact
paragraphs: Record quality directly affects security workflow prioritization and dashboard interpretation. Missing or inaccurate ownership metadata weakens escalation and delays remediation decisions.
Treat record corrections as first-order risk reduction. The Security and Dashboard modules become materially more useful when Records data stays current.
